text: Ten lessons ago, this started as a one-sentence hallway question: can you tell me how we did yesterday? This lesson recaps everything that question turned into, and where it goes next.

You turned a vague ask into a specific requirement, planned the Bronze, Silver, Gold layers in plain English, landed raw POS and online data untouched in Bronze, cleaned and deduplicated it into Silver, aggregated Silver into a one-row-per-day Gold table, validated row counts across all three layers, scheduled the whole thing to run itself every morning, connected Power BI in Import mode, and presented the one number this project was actually asked for.

Strip away the retail example, and what's left is the real, transferable skill set: requirements clarification before code, the medallion architecture pattern, reading and writing Delta tables, a correct deduplication and aggregation, validating a pipeline's own correctness instead of trusting it ran, scheduling dependent tasks, and connecting a BI tool to the result. That list is the actual deliverable here.

And one more time, honestly: this pipeline rebuilds Silver and Gold from scratch every single run, with no incremental loading, and it serves exactly one stakeholder with one question. Both were named back in lesson one, and naming them again now is the same discipline lesson nine taught for handling a live follow-up question — a project you can't honestly describe the limits of isn't one you've fully understood.

That's exactly where the next project in this track picks up: a second stakeholder with a different question, reconciled against the same source data, and incremental loading with Delta's merge, updating only what's new each run instead of rebuilding everything from scratch. You've built the first, smallest real medallion pipeline — the next one builds on it directly.
